outlook.statement: Completion of the renovation and expansion project, including the addition of new guest rooms and upgradation of existing facilities, will significantly enhance the Company's operational capabilities and competitive positioning. These strategic investments are expected to improve guest experience, increase occupancy levels, strengthen revenue generation, and support sustainable growth and long-term profitability.

The outlook for India's hospitality sector remains positive supported by sustained growth in domestic tourism. The ongoing renovation and expansion of the hotel is expected to improve occupancy levels, increase average room revenue, and strengthen competitive position, leading to improved revenues, enhanced operational efficiencies, and sustained profitability in coming years.

The hospitality sector is expected to remain stable in FY 2026-27, supported by domestic leisure travel and MICE demand, with room rates likely to remain firm. Industry revenues are projected to grow by ~7-9% Y-o-Y in FY 2026-27, with occupancy and ARR continuing to improve.

Over the medium to long term, structural drivers including rising discretionary spending, an expanding middle class and continued business travel are expected to support industry growth. India's rising prominence in the global economy is expected to contribute to sectoral growth by attracting higher inflows of foreign visitors.

The Company believes that the ongoing renovation of the hotel, together with the addition of new guest rooms and the upgradation of existing facilities, will significantly enhance its operational capacity and overall guest experience. These initiatives are expected to improve occupancy levels, increase average room revenue, and strengthen the Company's competitive position in the hospitality sector.
Your Company has also taken various initiatives to improve sales and optimize costs to improve profitability in the forthcoming years.

The elevation and renovation of the hotel property continuing to sustain the operations in hospitality industry. During the financial year, the Company completed renovation of rooms and the related capex has been capitalised.

key_audit_matters: Carrying value of the right-of-use asset and measurement of the lease liability - The Company operates its hotel on land leased from the Airports Authority of India. As at March 31, 2026 the Company carries a right-of-use asset of INR 3,018.55 lakhs against lease liabilities of INR 3,782.40 lakhs, and the unwinding of the discount on the lease liability of INR 440.07 lakhs is the single largest charge in the statement of profit and loss. Measurement of the lease liability and of the related right-of-use asset is governed by Ind AS 116 — Leases and, where indicators of impairment exist, by Ind AS 36 — Impairment of Assets. Significant management judgement is involved in determining the lease term, the incremental borrowing rate used to discount the lease payments, and whether the losses incurred in the current and the preceding financial year constitute an indicator of impairment of the cash-generating unit to which the right-of-use asset and the related property, plant and equipment belong.
